_comment: Every setting re:dial reads, for the settings window's Every setting page. key is the dotted path in config.json; removing a key restores the default. tests/test_dial.py checks this list against the daemon and config.example.json, so a new setting without a row here fails the tests.

items.label: Design language
items.help: How the overlay is drawn and moves. re:dial classic is the standard; community languages appear here once installed in plugin/redial/languages/.

items.label: Colour
items.help: Light is ink on vellum. Match desktop takes the Omarchy theme's colours.

items.label: Reference lines
items.help: Construction lines, crosshair and registration marks behind the drawing.

items.label: Layout
items.help: The overlay's shape.

items.label: Overlay style (without Omarchy)
items.help: How redial-overlay draws the tool ring on KDE, COSMIC and other desktops without Omarchy. Omarchy uses Layout instead.

items.label: Dial face
items.help: Which face the Dial layout draws. Only Classic draws turning, hints and can't-act itself so far; the others use the desktop's OSD.

items.label: Position
items.help: Where the overlay sits on the screen.

items.label: Backing
items.help: Unset follows the face: Classic a rectangle, Gauge none, the others a disc.

items.label: Backing strength
items.help: Hairlines need contrast over busy windows.

items.label: Reduce motion
items.help: No sliding or scaling; the overlay still fades.

items.label: Accent colour
items.help: theme follows the colour scheme. A hex such as #c4452a or a theme slot color0 to color15 overrides it.

items.label: Ink colour
items.help: theme follows the colour scheme; a hex or theme slot overrides it.

items.label: Ground colour
items.help: theme follows the colour scheme; a hex or theme slot overrides it.

items.label: Callout note
items.help: The note a leader line points to: the tool, its click and its value.

items.label: Construction lines
items.help: Needs Reference lines on.

items.label: Crosshair
items.help: Needs Reference lines on.

items.label: Registration marks
items.help: Needs Reference lines on.

items.label: Capsule rounding
items.help: Capsule face only.

items.label: Capsule width
items.help: Capsule face only.

items.label: Card width
items.help: Deck layout only.

items.label: Card height
items.help: Deck layout only.

items.label: Card gap
items.help: Deck layout only.

items.label: Sensitivity
items.help: Higher means less turning per step.

items.label: Return to Volume after
items.help: Scroll, Pages and Settings stay at least 60 s: you stop to read.

items.label: Return time per tool
items.help: Seconds for one tool, beating Return to Volume after: {"Scroll": 120, "Media": 30}.

items.label: Ignore small turns
items.help: Counts to turn after a pause before anything happens. Filters bumps and tremor.

items.label: Hold to open the tool menu
Tap menu
items.help: Let go once it opens, then turn and click to choose.

items.label: Show what turning does
items.help: Levels, window names and track position on screen.

items.label: Speak the tool name
items.help: Needs spd-say or espeak-ng.

items.label: Welcome dismissed
items.help: Off shows the welcome card again.

items.label: Overlay safety close
items.help: The overlay closes itself after this long if the daemon goes quiet.

items.label: Clicks for one tool
items.help: A tool's own single, double or triple click, beating its default and the clicks above: {"Pointer": {"triple": "copy"}}. "tool" is the tool's own click. Set on the Feel page.

items.label: Quick assistant
items.help: The command the Quick assistant click runs: {"label": "...", "cmd": ["..."]}.

items.label: Your launchers
items.help: Up to 12 click actions of your own: [{"name": "Notes", "cmd": ["obsidian"]}]. Restart the dial service after editing.

items.label: Tools on the ring
items.help: Names in ring order. The Look page edits this; empty means the default ring.

items.label: Custom tools
items.help: Full tool definitions for tools the library can't express. Wins over Tools on the ring. See config.example.json.
